messages:
kevin: pasted a perfetto / nsys timeline — seeing repeated cuBLASLt algo swaps across consecutive matmuls, latency jitter ~20-40ms :thinking:
maya: can you attach the nsys export? curious if workspace allocations line up with the flips
kevin: uploaded algo-flip.nsys.gz to the thread, note hotspots at kernel idx 42/43, and a big cudaMalloc spike right before the slower kernel
rachel: batching heuristics might be causing shape churn — if the batcher mixes short and long sequences we hit different split-K / algo choices
kevin: right, this run used batcher=v2 with dynamic padding. here's the snippet from the nsys markups:
```
[NSYS] Range: matmul_forward
[CUFFT] cublasLtMatmul (algoId=1, wspace=0)
[CUFFT] cublasLtMatmul (algoId=5, wspace=912384)
[CUDA] cudaMalloc 912384
[CUFFT] cublasLtMatmul (algoId=1, wspace=0)
```
maya: that alternating wspace sizes smell like split-K fallback vs batched algo. when wspace>0 it selects algo that needs workspace, otherwise it picks a different algo
diego: also check kv-cache warmup — if prefix KV cache is being restored it can change effective sequence length, which affects matmul shapes
kevin: good call — KV warmup logs show a bunch of lookups around the same time as the cudaMallocs. maybe cache warmstart mis-scheduled into the serving threads
rachel: could be a thread-affinity problem. if the cache population runs on the same GPU worker while another req gets scheduled, we might see transient fragmentation and allocation stalls
maya: can we reproduce with a controlled trace? suggest running with NVTX scopes around batcher boundaries and force two shape classes in replay
diego: repro command I used for local trace:
```
nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --output=algoflip-local ./tests/replay_workload --shape-classes "short,long" --batcher dynamic
```
kevin: ran that, reproduced. perf timeline shows 3 flips in 20s. attaching thread snapshot.
infra-bot: deployment "staging-serving/3" CPU/GPU autoscaler triggered extra worker during trace (scale event 1717654480)
rachel: autoscale event could explain extra concurrent work. if new worker pulled model with different cuBLASLt heuristics it might affect placement or memory layout
maya: workaround: pin batcher to stable padding for a minute during warmup and pre-allocate a small workspace pool to avoid cudaMalloc spikes
diego: we should also add a guard in runtime: if cudaMalloc latency > Xms then prefer non-wspace algo for the next N requests to avoid jitter
kevin: +1. will open a short PR with NVTX ranges and a repro script, and a perf regression test that checks for repeated algo flips under controlled shapes
rachel: add test that runs against both quantized/float models — quantization changes kernel selection heuristics
kevin: filing the issue now: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2146 — tags: eng-runtime, perf, cublaslt
maya: nice. for the PR also include a small micro-benchmark that demonstrates latency delta between algoId=1 and algoId=5 across batch sizes
diego: leaving a note to check fragmentation via cudaMemGetInfo during repro too, helps correlate free/used peaks
kevin: thanks all, repro artifacts and nsys exports uploaded in the ticket. will follow up with PR link when ready :thumbsup:
